findings.premise: The writer inventory is complete enough to ensure that every review publication and artifact rewrite preserves presentation and approval state.
findings.evidence: The design names run-artifact.ts for review publication, but controller reviews independently publish in findings.ts and verdicts.ts: both call 'writeAtomic(state.jsonPath, ... review: report ...)'. Code reviews publish through runner.ts using 'deps.write(paths.json, ...)' followed by the markdown write. Additionally, appendFeedbackBatch reads an entire artifact and calls writeArtifactJson, which uses writeFileSync without the approval lock. These omitted writers can bypass lastReviewWriteAt stamping or overwrite newly written presentation/approval metadata across workers. findings.premise: Timestamp-based presentation freshness ensures that the human opened the state being approved despite a concurrent review publication.
findings.evidence: Client content retrieval and presentation are separate operations. docs-review-client.ts fetches workflow.artifactContent, which returns renderedMarkdown and contentVersion; JetBrains likewise fetches content before rendering it. The proposed workflow.present accepts only documents and sessionId, with no viewed version. If a review publishes after content retrieval but before presentation stamping, presentedAt exceeds lastReviewWriteAt and approval passes while the client displays the earlier content. The lock around the stamp cannot detect that stale read. findings.action: Specify a version-bound read/present protocol that verifies the displayed artifact/review revision under the writer lock, and require reopening when it changed. Cover the read → review-publication → presentation → approval race.

summary.prose: The daemon refuses approvals that were never presented to the human first, enforced in the one shared approve path (approveArtifactByJsonPath) with single-use, TTL-bound, fingerprint-safe presentation records. Every writer of approval-relevant state — approve, reject, review publication, review resolution, present stamp, AMD transition — runs under one per-artifact cross-worker lock with a final reread, so no stale snapshot can overwrite a newer approval, rejection, review or token. Presentation freshness is judged against an authoritative lastReviewWriteAt marker stamped at review/code-review publication completion. insrc_present becomes a write (workflow.present) wired into every approval surface at document-open time: the MCP tool, VS Code docs review, the JetBrains review pane, and a new TUI open-and-read view whose approve action is enabled only by a fresh presentation. epicHash batch approval requires the explicit artifactIds list. AMD amendments are gated through approveAmendment with approvedBy attribution preserved. Review gates — including the non-overridable stale-review fingerprint rule — are untouched.
